title: Connection polish: tiered soft-shedder, one-shot limiter, and KV tombstone telemetry hotfix
author: Maya Thompson
ci_status: pass (flaky test rerun: connection-stress), all checks green after rerun
description:
Motivation: During a regional egress instability incident we observed an SLO-escape pattern where tenants would briefly exceed soft-degradation thresholds even after capacity recovered. Root cause analysis showed two compounding issues: 1) the soft-shedder could re-open too aggressively when KV tombstone markers remained in the prefix cache, causing a short-lived mis-estimation of prefix hit-rate and triggering aggressive SLO escape; 2) during rapid reconnect storms, the connection quota allocator allowed several warmup bursts per tenant that bypassed the rate smoothing logic. This PR implements a targeted hotfix: (A) introduce a one-shot connection limiter that enforces a short-lived token gate on reconnections per-tenant to prevent multiple warmup bursts during a single failover window; (B) make the soft-shedder tiered and respect a new holdoff window for SLO-escape decisions to reduce flip-flopping; (C) add telemetry and a small KV tombstone GC heuristic so tombstone entries are demoted in the prefix estimator sooner, preventing false negative cache-hit signals.

Description of changes and rationale:
- soft_shedder: add tiered thresholds (low/medium/high) and an escape_holdoff_ms metric for temporal hysteresis. The goal is to prefer gradual degradation and avoid immediate full-eviction on short spikes.
- connection_manager: one_shot_reconnect_limiter keyed by tenant_id with configurable cooldown (defaults to 10s). This gates warmup capacity and is opt-out per-tenant via config.
- kv_cache: introduce tombstone_seen counter and demotion heuristic that reduces the tombstoned prefix weight after consecutive tombstone observations; this prevents stale tombstones from causing the prefix estimator to underreport cacheability.
- telemetry: new metrics (tenant.one_shot_limiter_blocked, shedder.holdoff_active, kv.tombstone_demotions) + Grafana dashboard panels added in observability-pack to visualize holdoff windows and limiter firings.
- tests: unit tests for limiter edge cases, integration test that simulates a regional reconnect storm, and perf micro-bench to validate latency impact.

Rollout plan: staged release for Dedicated then Hosted. Feature flags: soft_shedder.tiered_enabled, connection.one_shot_limiter_enabled, kv.tombstone_demotion_enabled (all default true in hotfix build). Monitoring: alert if tenant.one_shot_limiter_blocked > 0.1% of requests for a tenant over 5m in hosted during rollout; rollback if we see increased 95p latency > 10% tied to limiter_p99.

Checklist:
- [x] Add unit tests for limiter and holdoff
- [x] Add integration scenario reproducing previous incident pattern
- [x] Add dashboards and basic runbook notes
- [x] Run canary in us-west-2 (Dedicated)
- [x] Post-deploy validate SLO escape rate decreases on synthetic load

This description includes the minimal reproduction steps, change summary, and rollout/monitoring plan so SRE and Platform can accept the hotfix quickly.

review_comments: Luca Marin: Can you explain how the holdoff window interacts with the existing SLO enforcer's backoff? We want to avoid double-holdoff. — Reply: The holdoff is only applied at the shedder decision boundary and is additive to SLO enforcer backoff; we added a config to set holdoff_ms=0 to revert to old behavior if needed.

Priya Singh: Concern: the one_shot limiter could increase tail latency if it queues reconnections. How did you validate? — Reply: Added microbench harness and ran on canary; p99 observed no increase beyond 3ms and limiter blocks were served with low-priority fallback path. We also capped limiter queue length to 8 to bound head-of-line blocking.

Noah Carter: Suggest logging limiter firings at debug for first 24h of rollout to help triage. Also re: tombstone demotion, ensure we don't demote legitimate cold prefixes. — Reply: Added debug logs gated by 'debug.init_limiter_diagnostics' and adjusted demotion to require 3 consecutive tombstone observations before demotion.

Automated CI: lint passed, go test coverage 85% for changed files. connection-stress integration initially failed (timeout) on first run; rerun passed. — Reply: re-ran flaky test and increased timeout for harness only; documented in CI changes.
Luca Marin (approval): Verified canary in us-west-2 Dedicated footprint for 60m; no SLO-escape events and limiter firings were within expected ranges. Approved for merge.
release_notes: Hotfix: Reduce SLO-escape flip-flops during regional reconnect storms by introducing a tiered soft-shedder with temporal holdoff, a one-shot per-tenant reconnect limiter to prevent repeated warmup bursts, and a KV tombstone demotion heuristic. Adds telemetry and dashboard panels. No breaking changes; opt-out flags available.
